@graph.name: Carton Palletizer
@graph.description: A carton palletizer is a robotic system that stacks closed paperboard or corrugated cartons onto pallets in stable layers, using grippers and pallet patterns that protect printed surfaces and carton strength. TRF Industrial Automation builds carton palletizers on TRFCobot, TRFCompact and TRFSpeed, or as a custom palletizer, and the right model is defined by your line setup and speed.

mainEntity.name: Can a Carton Palletizer Fit a Plant With Limited Floor Space?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. TRFCobot has a small footprint for areas where a traditional robotic cell is hard to install, and TRFCompact brings an industrial robot into a compact, standardized cell for brownfield plants and secondary lines. The area for the robot, the infeed pick point, the pallet positions and operator access to full pallets is confirmed with your layout, together with the robot reach.

mainEntity.name: What Payload Does a Palletizing Robot Need for Cartons?

acceptedAnswer.text: The robot must carry the carton plus the end-of-arm tool, and for multipick, the combined weight of all cartons in the pick. Published case weights are up to about 22 lb for TRFCobot, 44 lb for TRFCompact and 66 lb for TRFSpeed. TRF validates the final payload with your cartons, tool, pick count and pallet pattern.

mainEntity.name: Can a Carton Palletizer Be Integrated With My Cartoner, Conveyors and Wrapper?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The palletizer needs cartons closed, square and spaced, with glue set so flaps do not open under the tool. TRFIntraflow provides accumulation, metering, gapping, merging and routing between the cartoner and the robot, and end-of-line integration ties cartoning, palletizing, wrapping and labeling into one project with one partner.

mainEntity.name: Can a Robotic Palletizer Operate Below Freezing for Frozen Food Cartons?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, with TRFSubzero, the TRF palletizer for areas below 32°F, built for frozen food, ice cream and other below-freezing areas. Rate, payload and end-of-arm tool for frozen cartons are validated per application, and the frozen food and ice cream page shows how palletizing fits a cold-chain end of line.

mainEntity.name: How Much Does a Carton Palletizer Cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cost depends on the platform, carton rate, picks per cycle, end-of-arm tool, pallet and sheet handling and conveyor integration. As a reference, list prices are US$ 120,000 for the TRFCobot Dual, US$ 180,000 for the TRFCompact Dual and US$ 350,000 for the TRFSpeed 100, EX Works Lenexa, Kansas, installation not included. The robotic palletizer cost page explains each factor.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Typical Payback Period for a Robotic Palletizer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Payback depends on the labor hours the palletizer replaces, shifts per day, local labor cost and the installed cost of the system. The palletizing ROI calculator applies this method to your location, your shifts and the people who palletize by hand today. On carton lines, also note the effects it does not measure directly, such as gentler handling and consistent patterns.

mainEntity.name: What Information Should I Prepare to Size a Carton Palletizer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bring your carton sizes and weights, board type, print and label locations, carton rate at peak, SKU list and changeover frequency, shifts per day, pallet size and target height, and a drawing of the end of the line. A TRF Sales Engineer uses this data to screen TRFCobot, TRFCompact, TRFSpeed or a custom palletizer and validate the fit.
